shinyOAuth 0.8.0 release checks

Source: .github/release-0.8.0.md

Prepared on 2026-11-17 using the R Packages release guide.

The local checks use isolated libraries, including openssl 2.6.0, S7 0.2.2, otel 0.3.0 and otelsdk 0.3.0. The R 4.6.2 library also uses current CRAN versions of the other dependencies.

The manual is built separately because the check commands use --no-manual. Browser and provider integration tests run in the repository’s integration CI; the full local suite disables browser tests explicitly.

The reference CI run predates the 0.8.0 version bump. Relative to that commit, the candidate’s R code differs only by the new discovery example in roxygen comments, and NAMESPACE is unchanged. One telemetry unit test now mocks SDK span completion and verifies cleanup for both success and error outcomes. The complete 0.8.0 source archive is checked locally on both Windows R versions.

The reverse-dependency comparison uses the CRAN Windows binary of 0.7.0 and the built 0.8.0 source candidate in separate libraries. Both runs use the same dependency versions. The optional, non-CRAN arcgisbinding package is unavailable in both environments.

The existing deprecated request aliases continue to point users to their replacements; no further deprecation stage is advanced in this release.

The test additions since 0.7.0 were reviewed again for CRAN portability. Five of the six new test files are outside the CRAN selection. The remaining file keeps small independent-decryption, forged-state rejection and legacy-state rejection checks. Its exhaustive mutations, exact-byte checks and diagnostic output checks run only in the full suite. New subprocess, exact 1 MiB boundary, backend-error and serialization-dependent callback checks also skip on CRAN. The crypto fixture is static data and does not require Python.

Fresh CRAN-mode checks on both Windows R versions pass 2,972 assertions with nine deliberate skips and no failures or warnings. A separate check explicitly including the backend file confirms its file-level CRAN skip. The affected tests still pass all 900 assertions in full mode without warnings or skips.
